en: And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Yahya ibn Habib narrated to me: Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us; both of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of transmission; and in the hadith of Yahya: 'with its haunch or its two thighs.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were passing by Marr az-Zahran and startled a hare. They chased it until they grew exhausted. He said: Then I ran until I caught it, and brought it to Abu Talhah, who slaughtered it and sent its haunch and its two thighs to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). So I brought them to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he accepted it.

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far; both of them from Shu'bah, from Abu Ya'fur, with this chain of transmission, and he said: 'seven expeditions.'

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar all narrated it from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Abu Ya'fur, with this chain of transmission. Abu Bakr said in his narration: 'seven expeditions,' Ishaq said: 'six,' and Ibn Abi 'Umar said: 'six or seven.'

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Ya'fur, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: We went on seven military expeditions with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), eating locusts.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Abu 'Aqil ad-Dawraqi narrated to us: Abu Nadrah narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id: that a Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'I live in a low ground full of mastigures (spiny-tailed lizards), and they are the staple food of my family.' He said: But he did not answer him. So we said: 'Ask him again.' He asked him again, but he did not answer him three times. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out to him on the third time, saying: 'O Bedouin, indeed Allah cursed—or became angry with—a tribe of the Children of Israel, and transformed them into beasts creeping upon the earth. I do not know, perhaps this is among them; so I do not eat it, nor do I forbid it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are in a land abundant with mastigures (spiny-tailed lizards); what do you command us, or what ruling do you give us?' He said: 'It was mentioned to me that a community from the Children of Israel was transformed.' So he neither commanded nor forbade. Abu Sa'id said: Sometime after that, 'Umar said: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings benefit through it to more than one person, and it is the staple food of most of these shepherds; and if I had some with me, I would have eaten it. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) only felt a distaste for it.'

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, who said: I asked Jabir about the mastigure (spiny-tailed lizard), and he said: 'Do not eat it,' and he found it repulsive. And he said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not forbid it. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings benefit through it to more than one person, and indeed it is the food of most of the shepherds; and if I had some with me, I would have eaten it.'

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Abd ar-Razzaq reported to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Abu az-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: A mastigure (spiny-tailed lizard) was brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), but he refused to eat from it, saying: 'I do not know; perhaps it is from the generations that were transformed.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from ash-Shaybani, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, who said: A newly married man invited us in Medina and served us thirteen mastigures; some ate and some refrained. The next day, I met Ibn 'Abbas and informed him, and the people around him began to talk a lot until some of them said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'I neither eat it, nor do I forbid it, nor do I declare it unlawful.' Ibn 'Abbas said: 'How evil is what you have said! The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was sent only to declare lawful and unlawful. While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was with Maymunah, and with him were al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas, Khalid ibn al-Walid, and another woman, a dining table with meat on it was brought to them. When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was about to eat, Maymunah said to him: 'It is mastigure meat.' So he withdrew his hand and said: 'This is meat that I have never eaten.' And he said to them: 'Eat.' So al-Fadl, Khalid ibn al-Walid, and the woman ate from it. And Maymunah said: 'I will not eat from anything except what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) eats from.'

Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us—Ibn Nafi' said: Ghundar reported to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas saying: My maternal aunt Umm Hufayd gifted clarified butter (ghee), dried curd (iqit), and mastigures to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He ate from the clarified butter and dried curd, and left the mastigures out of personal distaste; and they were eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and had it been unlawful, it would not have been eaten at the table of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

Abu Bakr ibn an-Nadr and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—'Abd said: he reported to me, and Abu Bakr said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl, from Ibn 'Abbas: that he informed him that Khalid ibn al-Walid informed him that he entered with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) upon Maymunah bint al-Harith, and she was his maternal aunt. Meat of mastigure was presented to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), which Umm Hufayd bint al-Harith had brought from Najd—and she was married to a man from Banu Ja'far—and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would rarely eat anything until he knew what it was. Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Yunus, and added at the end of the hadith: and Ibn al-Asamm narrated it from Maymunah, and he was under her guardianship.

Abu at-Tahir and Harmalah both narrated to me from Ibn Wahb—Harmalah said: Ibn Wahb reported to us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf al-Ansari: that 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas informed him that Khalid ibn al-Walid—who is called the Sword of Allah—informed him that he entered with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) upon Maymunah, wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and she was his maternal aunt and maternal aunt of Ibn 'Abbas. He found with her a roasted mastigure which her sister Hufaydah bint al-Harith had brought from Najd. She presented the mastigure to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and food was seldom presented to him without it being described and named for him. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) reached out his hand towards the mastigure, whereupon one of the women present said: 'Inform the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) of what you have presented to him.' They said: 'It is mastigure, O Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) raised his hand, so Khalid ibn al-Walid asked: 'Is mastigure unlawful, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, but it was not in the land of my people, so I find that I have a distaste for it.' Khalid said: 'So I pulled it towards myself and ate it while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was looking on, and he did not forbid me.'

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from my grandfather: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal narrated to me, from Ibn al-Munkadir: that Abu Umamah ibn Sahl informed him from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Mastigure meat was brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while he was in the house of Maymunah, and Khalid ibn al-Walid was with him. Then he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of az-Zuhri.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Razzaq reported to us: Ma'mar reported to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Two roasted mastigures were brought to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while we were in the house of Maymunah. With the like of their hadith, and he did not mention Yazid ibn al-Asamm from Maymunah.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I recited to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: Khalid ibn al-Walid and I entered with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) the house of Maymunah, and a roasted mastigure was brought. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) reached out his hand towards it, whereupon some of the women in Maymunah's house said: 'Inform the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) what he intends to eat.' So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) raised his hand. I said: 'Is it unlawful, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, but it was not in the land of my people, so I find that I have a distaste for it.' Khalid said: 'So I pulled it towards myself and ate it while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was looking on.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Tawbah al-'Anbari, who said: ash-Sha'bi said to me: 'Have you considered the hadith of al-Hasan from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)? Yet I sat with Ibn 'Umar for nearly two years, or a year and a half, and I did not hear him narrate from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) other than this.' He said: 'There were people among the companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), among whom was Sa'd...' with the like of the hadith of Mu'adh.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Tawbah al-'Anbari, who heard ash-Sha'bi, who heard Ibn 'Umar: that some people among the companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), among whom was Sa'd, were with him, and meat of mastigure was brought to them. Then one of the wives of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out: 'It is mastigure meat.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Eat, for it is lawful, but it is not of my food.'

Abu ar-Rabi' and Qutaybah narrated it to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Isma'il narrated to us; both of them from Ayyub; (Third Chain) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us; (Fourth Chain) and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Bakr reported to us: Ibn Jurayj reported to us; (Fifth Chain) and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us: Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: I heard Musa ibn 'Uqbah; (Sixth Chain) and Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah informed me; all of them from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) regarding the mastigure, with the meaning of the hadith of al-Layth from Nafi', except that in the hadith of Ayyub: 'A mastigure was brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he neither ate it nor forbade it'; and in the hadith of Usamah: he said: 'A man stood up in the mosque while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was on the pulpit.'
'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Yahya narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah, the like of it with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while he was on the pulpit about eating the mastigure, and he said: 'I neither eat it nor do I forbid it.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to me: al-Layth reported to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about eating the mastigure, and he said: 'I neither eat it nor do I forbid it.'

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated from Isma'il—Yahya ibn Yahya said: Isma'il ibn Ja'far reported to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar: that he heard Ibn 'Umar saying: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was asked about the mastigure, and he said: 'I am not an eater of it, nor one who forbids it.'

And Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Abu Mu'awiyah reported to us; (Second Chain) and Abu Kuraib narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; both of them from Hisham, with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father, Hafs ibn Ghiyath, and Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham, from Fatimah, from Asma', who said: We slaughtered a horse during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and ate it.

And Abu at-Tahir narrated it to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us; (Second Chain) and Ya'qub ad-Dawraqi and Ahmad ibn 'Uthman an-Nawfali narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us; both of them from Ibn Jurayj, with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj reported to us: Abu az-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: At the time of Khaybar, we ate horses and wild asses, and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade us from domestic donkeys.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu ar-Rabi' al-'Ataki, and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id—and the wording is that of Yahya—narrated to us; Yahya said: he reported to us, and the other two said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade on the day of Khaybar the meat of domestic donkeys and permitted the meat of horses.

Muhammad ibn Minhal ad-Darir narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When it was the day of Khaybar, a comer came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the donkeys have been eaten.' Then another came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the donkeys have been consumed.' Thereupon, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered Abu Talhah, who announced: 'Indeed, Allah and His Messenger forbid you from the meat of donkeys, for it is impure (or unclean).' He said: So the pots were overturned with whatever was in them.

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Anas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) conquered Khaybar, we captured donkeys outside the village and cooked from them. Then the caller of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called out: 'Behold! Indeed Allah and His Messenger forbid you from them, for they are impure, of the work of Satan.' So the cooking pots were overturned with whatever was in them, while they were indeed boiling with their contents.
